rw-ii-central.name: Find the main point
steps: Read the whole passage before looking at choices.
Say the main point in one short sentence.
Pick the choice that matches your sentence, not just one detail.
Cut choices that are too broad or too narrow.
rw-ii-central.trap: Choosing an answer that is true for one sentence but not the whole passage.

rw-ii-evidence.name: Claim, then proof
steps: Underline the exact claim the question wants supported.
Restate that claim in your own words.
Test each choice: does it prove this claim directly?
For graphs, check the labels, units, and the exact numbers.
rw-ii-evidence.trap: Picking a true statement or real data point that does not support the specific claim.

rw-ii-inference.name: Smallest step
steps: Find the last line before the blank and what it sets up.
Predict what must logically come next.
Pick the choice that requires the fewest new assumptions.
Cut anything the text never actually supports.
rw-ii-inference.trap: Choosing an exciting conclusion that goes further than the text allows.

rw-cs-words.name: Predict the word
steps: Cover the choices and read the full sentence.
Say your own word for the blank using clues nearby.
Match your word to the choice closest in meaning.
Plug your pick back in and reread the sentence.
rw-cs-words.trap: Picking a familiar word that fits the topic but not this sentence's meaning.

rw-cs-structure.name: Job, not content
steps: Read the question to see which part it asks about.
Ask what that part does: claim, example, contrast, or detail.
Describe that job in a few words before reading choices.
Pick the choice whose verb matches the job you named.
rw-cs-structure.trap: Choosing an answer that summarizes what the text says instead of what it does.

rw-cs-cross.name: Pin both views
steps: Read Text 1 and write its view in five words.
Read Text 2 and write its view in five words.
Decide if they agree, disagree, or one qualifies the other.
Pick the choice that fits both of your notes.
rw-cs-cross.trap: Mixing up which author said what, or ignoring the second text's twist.

rw-ei-rhetorical.name: Goal first
steps: Read the question's goal before reading any notes.
Circle the key words of that goal.
Pick the choice that does exactly that goal.
Ignore choices that are accurate but serve a different goal.
rw-ei-rhetorical.trap: Choosing a sentence that uses correct facts from the notes but misses the stated goal.

rw-ei-transitions.name: Name the relationship
steps: Read the sentence before and the sentence after.
Label the link: add, contrast, cause, example, or sequence.
Cut every choice from a different category.
Pick the remaining word that fits the exact shade.
rw-ei-transitions.trap: Picking a transition that sounds smooth but signals the wrong relationship.

rw-sec-boundaries.name: Label both sides
steps: Find where the punctuation goes in the sentence.
Label each side: complete sentence or not.
Two complete sides need a period, semicolon, or comma plus conjunction.
Recheck: a lone comma between two complete sentences is wrong.
rw-sec-boundaries.trap: Accepting a comma splice because the sentence reads naturally aloud.

rw-sec-form.name: Find the true subject
steps: Cross out phrases between the subject and the verb.
Match the verb to the real subject in number and tense.
Check every pronoun points clearly to one noun.
Make sure a modifier sits right next to what it describes.
rw-sec-form.trap: Matching the verb to the nearest noun instead of the actual subject.

math-alg-linear-eq.name: Isolate cleanly
steps: Write down exactly what the question asks you to find.
Undo addition or subtraction first, then multiplication or division.
Flip the inequality sign if you multiply or divide by a negative.
Check whether they want x or an expression like 2x.
math-alg-linear-eq.trap: Solving for x when the question asked for a different expression.

math-alg-linear-fn.name: Slope and start
steps: Find the starting value: the y-intercept.
Find the rate: change in y over change in x.
Say the slope in words with units.
Match to the choice or graph with that start and rate.
math-alg-linear-fn.trap: Swapping slope and intercept, or reading rise over run upside down.

math-alg-systems.name: Line up and eliminate
steps: Write both equations with variables in the same order.
Pick the variable with the easiest coefficients to cancel.
Add or subtract to remove it, then solve.
Plug back in to find the other value.
math-alg-systems.trap: Stopping after finding one variable when the question asks for the other or a sum.

math-adv-quadratics.name: Pick the right form
steps: Ask what they want: roots, vertex, or y-intercept.
Use factored form for roots, vertex form for max or min.
Use standard form's constant for the y-intercept.
Check signs: (x - 3) means the root is positive 3.
math-adv-quadratics.trap: Getting the sign of a root or vertex coordinate backwards.

math-adv-nonlinear.name: Add or multiply?
steps: Check how the output changes each step.
Same amount added means linear; same factor multiplied means exponential.
Write the starting value and the growth or decay factor.
Plug in a simple input to confirm your model.
math-adv-nonlinear.trap: Treating a percent growth as a flat amount added each period.

math-adv-expressions.name: Simplify, then compare
steps: Factor or expand both sides to the simplest form.
Find a common denominator before combining fractions.
Note values that make a denominator zero.
Test a small number like 2 if the algebra stalls.
math-adv-expressions.trap: Canceling terms across addition instead of only common factors.

math-psda-ratios.name: Units guide you
steps: Write each number with its units.
Set up the ratio so units cancel to the answer's unit.
Cross multiply or scale up, then compute.
Check the answer's size makes sense for the story.
math-psda-ratios.trap: Flipping a rate so the units end up upside down.

math-psda-percent.name: Original times multiplier
steps: Identify the original amount the percent is based on.
Convert the change to a multiplier, like 1.15 or 0.80.
Multiply in order for back-to-back changes.
For percent change, divide the difference by the original.
math-psda-percent.trap: Adding successive percents or dividing by the new value instead of the original.

math-psda-stats.name: Count what matters
steps: Identify what the question wants: mean, median, range, or probability.
For probability, put the favorable count over the right total.
For mean, check if an outlier shifts it more than the median.
Read table rows and columns twice before dividing.
math-psda-stats.trap: Using the whole table's total when the question limits it to one group.

math-psda-inference.name: Read the model honestly
steps: Read the axis labels and units first.
Use the line of best fit for predictions, not single dots.
Interpret slope as the change in y per one unit of x.
Only generalize to the group that was randomly sampled.
math-psda-inference.trap: Claiming cause and effect, or applying a sample's result to a different population.

math-geo-area.name: Draw and label
steps: Sketch the figure and label every given value.
Write the formula before plugging in numbers.
Use angle rules: straight line 180, triangle 180, parallel lines.
Check the answer has the right units: square or cubic.
math-geo-area.trap: Using diameter for radius, or mixing area and perimeter.

math-geo-triangles.name: Triangle first
steps: Draw the right triangle and label opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse.
Look for special triangles: 3-4-5, 30-60-90, 45-45-90.
Pick the trig ratio or Pythagorean theorem that uses your knowns.
For circles, connect radius, diameter, and arc to the full circle.
math-geo-triangles.trap: Labeling opposite and adjacent from the wrong angle.

english-punct.name: What's on each side
steps: Find the punctuation mark being tested.
Label each side: full sentence, phrase, or list item.
Match the mark to the job, like semicolon for two sentences.
For apostrophes, ask who owns it and how many owners.
english-punct.trap: Adding commas wherever you would pause when speaking.

english-grammar.name: Strip to the core
steps: Cross out the words between the subject and verb.
Match the verb to the subject and keep the tense consistent.
Check each pronoun matches its noun in number.
Make sure the modifier is next to what it describes.
english-grammar.trap: Matching the verb to a nearby noun instead of the real subject.

english-sentence.name: One sentence test
steps: Find the main subject and verb.
Check that it can stand alone as a complete thought.
Fix run-ons by splitting or joining with proper punctuation.
Make list items match in form, like all -ing words.
english-sentence.trap: Accepting a fragment because it is long and sounds complete.

english-strategy.name: Does it earn its place
steps: Read the question to learn the writer's goal.
Reread the paragraph around the sentence in question.
Ask if the paragraph loses anything without it.
Pick the yes or no choice whose reason matches.
english-strategy.trap: Choosing yes or no correctly but picking the wrong reason.

english-organization.name: Fit both neighbors
steps: Read the sentence before and after the spot.
Name the link: contrast, cause, addition, or order.
Pick the transition or placement that fits both neighbors.
For moving sentences, look for words pointing back to something.
english-organization.trap: Picking a transition that fits the next sentence but not the previous one.

english-style.name: Shortest clear choice
steps: Check whether OMIT or the shortest choice keeps the meaning.
Cut choices that repeat an idea already stated.
Match the tone of the passage, not too casual or fancy.
Pick the most precise word that fits the sentence.
english-style.trap: Choosing a longer, fancier answer that says the same thing twice.

math-prealgebra.name: Units and order
steps: Write each number with its units.
Follow order of operations step by step.
Convert percents to decimals before multiplying.
Check the answer size makes sense.
math-prealgebra.trap: Taking a percent of the wrong base amount.

math-algebra.name: Isolate and check
steps: Write what the question asks you to find.
Undo operations in reverse order to isolate the variable.
Flip an inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative.
Plug your answer back in to check.
math-algebra.trap: Forgetting to flip the inequality sign with a negative.

math-functions.name: Know the form
steps: Identify the function type: linear, quadratic, or exponential.
Use the form that shows what they ask for.
For f(g(x)), work from the inside out.
Plug in a test value to confirm your choice.
math-functions.trap: Doing the outer function first in a composition.

math-geometry.name: Sketch and formula
steps: Draw the figure and label all given values.
Write the formula from memory, no sheet provided.
Look for hidden triangles or right angles.
Check units and whether they want area or perimeter.
math-geometry.trap: Using diameter in place of radius.

math-coordinate.name: Slope first
steps: Plot or sketch the points given.
Find the slope between key points.
Use slope to answer parallel, perpendicular, or line questions.
For distance or midpoint, label x and y carefully.
math-coordinate.trap: Using the same slope for perpendicular lines instead of the negative reciprocal.

math-trig.name: Draw the triangle
steps: Draw the triangle and mark the angle in question.
Label opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse from that angle.
Pick sine, cosine, or tangent that uses your known sides.
Check your calculator is in the correct angle mode.
math-trig.trap: Labeling sides from the wrong angle.

math-stats.name: Favorable over total
steps: Decide if the question is mean, median, probability, or counting.
For probability, write favorable outcomes over total outcomes.
For counting, multiply the choices for each slot.
Check whether order matters before finishing.
math-stats.trap: Adding choices that should be multiplied, or using the wrong total.

math-modeling.name: Words to equation
steps: Underline what the question asks for.
Translate each sentence into math, one piece at a time.
Solve step by step and write each result.
Check the answer fits the story and units.
math-modeling.trap: Answering an earlier step instead of the final question.

reading-detail.name: Go back to the line
steps: Pick out the key words in the question.
Find those words in the passage.
Reread a few lines before and after.
Pick the choice that paraphrases those lines.
reading-detail.trap: Answering from memory and picking a choice with passage words but the wrong meaning.

reading-inference.name: Prove it in the text
steps: Find the lines the question points to.
Ask what the author clearly suggests there.
Cut choices you cannot back with a specific line.
Pick the most moderate supported choice.
reading-inference.trap: Picking an extreme answer that goes beyond what the author suggests.

reading-craft.name: Function and fit
steps: Reread the word or phrase in its full sentence.
Predict its meaning or job before reading choices.
Match your prediction to the choices.
Check tone words against the passage's overall attitude.
reading-craft.trap: Choosing the most common meaning of a word instead of its meaning in context.

reading-integration.name: Compare both texts
steps: Write each passage's main view in a few words.
Note where they agree and where they differ.
Check which passage the question asks about.
Pick the choice that fits both notes.
reading-integration.trap: Choosing a statement true of one passage when the question asks about both.

science-data.name: Labels then lookup
steps: Read the question first to see which figure it needs.
Read the axis labels and units on that figure.
Find the value or trend the question asks about.
Check your answer against the figure, not outside knowledge.
science-data.trap: Reading the wrong line, column, or unit on a figure.

science-research.name: Find what changed
steps: Identify what the experimenters changed on purpose.
Identify what they measured as the result.
Note what stayed the same in every trial.
Use those three roles to answer design questions.
science-research.trap: Mixing up the variable that was changed with the one that was measured.

science-conflict.name: Sort the views
steps: Read the intro for the question being debated.
Write each viewpoint's main claim in a few words.
Note where the viewpoints agree and disagree.
Answer by matching the claim to the right viewpoint.
science-conflict.trap: Attributing one scientist's claim to another.

general.name: Two passes
steps: First pass: answer every question you can do quickly.
Mark any question taking more than a minute and move on.
Second pass: return to marked questions with the time left.
Save the final minute to fill any blanks.

general.name: Cross out wrong answers
steps: Read every choice before picking one.
Cross out choices that are clearly wrong.
Compare the remaining choices word by word.
Guess from what is left if you are stuck.

general.name: Predict, then match
steps: Cover the choices after reading the question.
Say your own answer in a few words.
Find the choice closest to your prediction.

general.name: Read the question first
steps: Read the question before the passage or figure.
Note exactly what it asks for.
Read or look only where you need to.
Reread the question before choosing an answer.

general.name: Pick your own numbers
steps: Use when choices have variables in them.
Pick simple numbers like 2 or 3 for each variable.
Solve the problem with your numbers to get a target.
Plug the same numbers into each choice to find the match.

general.name: Work backward from choices
steps: Use when choices are numbers and the question asks for a value.
Start with a middle choice and test it in the problem.
If it is too big or small, move the right way.
Stop when one choice works.

general.name: Track units
steps: Write units next to every number you use.
Cancel units as you multiply or divide.
Check the final units match what the question asks.

general.name: Never leave a blank
steps: Wrong answers cost nothing, so answer every question.
Watch the clock and keep a minute in reserve.
Fill every blank with your best guess before time ends.
